doc.title: Candido Camero — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Jazz, Chano Pozo and Dizzy Gillespie
title: Jazz big bands heard in Cuba
summary: Basie, Ellington, Hampton, Herman, Dorsey and Miller were heard on Cuban radio, and he later worked with many of them.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: You told me in the first part of this interview yesterday that one of the foreign musics that was heard most during your childhood in Cuba, besides the tango, was jazz music.
Who were the artists that were heard at that time?

Well, the jazz orchestras - large orchestras such as Count Basie, Duke Ellington, Lionel Hampton, Woody Herman, Tommy Dorsey, Glen Miller . . . the orchestra of, let me see, Cab Calloway, Count Basie, Duke Ellington, Glen Miller, Tommy Dorsey, Harry James . . . All those big orchestras at that time were heard a lot on the radio there in Cuba.
Of those that you just named which influenced you the most?
All of them. They all had their different style and arrangements, and musicians. I was

fortunate enough to work and also recorded with Count Basie when I came here to the United States, with Count Basie, with Stan Kenton, Duke Ellington with Tommy Dorsey, with Woody Herman, with Buddy Rich - those were the bands that were heard there in Cuba.
